entities.summary: Hexameter is a literary work of ancient Greek origin, dating back to the 8th century BCE, with notable significance in its field. It holds the core of Western poetry and has influenced countless works throughout history. The core events of hexameter's development involved the creation of the ancient Greek epic poem, the Iliad and Odyssey, attributed to Homer and Sappho respectively. These poems showcased the use of the hexameter as a versatile poetic form. Hexameter's legacy is seen in the widespread adoption of its structure by Latin poets like Virgil and Ovid, who used it to great effect in their own works. The Roman poet Ovid's Metamorphoses, for instance, employs the hexameter extensively throughout its 15 books. Today, hexameter remains a staple of classical studies and continues to be studied and emulated by scholars and poets alike.
